newsitem.title: TAIWAN: July-Sept profits rise at Taiwan's Big Three banks.
newsitem.headline: July-Sept profits rise at Taiwan's Big Three banks.

text.p: Pre-tax profits of Taiwan's Big Three state-run banks rose in the July-September quarter compared with the third quarter of 1995, the Commercial Times newspaper said on Thursday.
First Bank's July-September pre-tax profit was T$1.839 billion, up a year-on-year 22.03 percent. Its earnings per share topped the two colleague banks at T$1.01, the paper said.
Hua Nan Bank reported pre-tax profit of T$1.552 billion, up 7.4 percent. Per share earnings were T$0.73.
Chang Hwa Bank had pre-tax profit of T$1.318 billion in the period, up a year-on-year 31.41 percent with per share earnings at T$0.8.
The banks' pre-tax profits in September were mixed, with two increasing and one declining.
In September, First Bank's pre-tax profit was T$604 million, up 12.89 percent from September 1995. Hua Nan's pre-tax profit was T$522 million, up 5.45 percent.
Chang Hwa Bank's pre-tax profit fell 19.36 percent to T$404 million.
